items.title: Rossano Sportiello interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 2, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Chopin could improvise a ballad you know, no problem.

ctx.x: Yeah. It’s clear and people have said that it’s like a language. I think the part that’s difficult is that the underlying chords as they shift, that you have to keep up with that.

Right. Well the other thing that we have to keep in mind is that when you are improvising it’s not really about throwing in right notes on top of chords. You have to act like you are a composer. It means that while improvising, okay, you say a phrase. You play a phrase. Then the next phrase should be kind of consequential, like to reaffirm what you just stated. And then you can keep going on on that kind of development of the same idea, up to a point, like you feel that it’s time to introduce a new element. It’s…
Hear it in your head. Yeah.
